mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility, moving from -42.9% to -38.6%, indicates a continuous recovery in consumer activity, which will persist and drive further increases over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM mobility approaches its pre-period baseline, currently at -0.4%, it signals a return to more normalized routines and increased comfort with out-of-home activities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -0.5, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A combined recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, both showing recent upward trends, indicates a broader return to office-based work and associated commuting, which will directly boost weekday retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their upward trend, RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility, currently at 22.6% and trending downwards, indicates fewer people staying home, freeing up time and inclination for out-of-home activities, thereby increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 22.0, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent 28 days, or even declines.

mechanism_narrative: The consistent upward trend in PARKS mobility, moving from -26.0% to -15.4%, often serves as an early indicator of increased comfort with public spaces, which will translate into higher RETAIL_REC as people extend their outdoor activities to include shopping and leisure over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility continues to rise, but RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or decreases over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant and sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility, indicated by a week-on-week increase exceeding 1 percentage point for two consecutive weeks, will drive a corresponding increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to increased weekday foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases by more than 1.0 point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES shows the specified increase, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the subsequent 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 24.3% to 22.6%) and an increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -4.3% to -0.4%) suggests a fundamental shift away from home-centric activities towards essential out-of-home errands, which will spill over into non-essential retail and recreation over the next one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat in the next 7 days despite RESIDENTIAL decreasing and GROCERY_PHARM increasing.

mechanism_narrative: Under stable or easing policy conditions, a consistent recovery in TRANSIT station visits, moving from -42.1% to -37.7%, indicates increased public transport usage, which directly facilitates access to retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues its upward trend, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, or policy conditions tighten significantly.
